subject: Post-demo: latency/throughput tradeoffs — Hosted vs Dedicated recommendation
messages:
From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@velocityai.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@velocityai.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up from demo — latency targets and QPS profile

Thanks for the demo earlier today — helpful walkthrough. A couple quick clarifications so we can align internally before we scope costs:

- Target P99 latency: <= 120ms for typical short prompts (<= 64 tokens) — this is for the customer-facing autocomplete path.
- Sustained throughput: planning for ~40 qps average, with burst capacity up to 200 qps during peak events.
- Session context: typical sessions are 1–2 requests per user, KV cache hits expected ~65%.
- Security: we need SOC2 evidence and confirmation that logs can be retained in our tenancy for up to 90 days (if Dedicated or Private).

We're leaning toward Dedicated capacity because predictable latency is a must, but open to a Hosted pilot if you can guarantee latency headroom during the pilot window and offer a clear migration path. Can you share: (1) an estimated Dedicated configuration (GPU count / instance types) that meets the P99 target at 200 qps burst, (2) a Hosted pilot plan with expected latencies and rollback/fallback behavior, and (3) a short mutual action plan we can use to get procurement moving?

Appreciate it —
Tim
Director of Product
VelocityAI

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Lee <tim.lee@velocityai.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@velocityai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from demo — latency targets and QPS profile

Hi Tim — thanks for the clear summary and the latency targets. Recap + proposed next steps below. I've attached a 1-page mutual action plan (velocity_map_v1.pdf) and a small "latency test instructions" doc we can run against Hosted so you get real numbers quickly.

Recap of asks (from your note):
- P99 <= 120ms for <=64 tokens (autocomplete).
- Avg 40 qps, burst 200 qps; KV cache hit ~65%.
- SOC2 evidence and 90-day log retention in tenancy (if using Dedicated/Private).

Our suggested approach:
1) Short Hosted pilot (2 weeks) — run the latency test guide against our Hosted API to collect baseline P50/P95/P99 under your traffic profile. Hosted gives fastest time to start and we can route pilot requests to nodes optimized for low-latency. We will: enable prefix caching and a small continuous-batching window tuned to your profile to reduce tail latency.
2) Parallel sizing exercise for Dedicated — Vivek will propose a Dedicated pool config that can meet 200 qps burst at your P99 target; we'll include cost estimates and a suggested canary rollout plan.
3) If latency after Hosted pilot is within a 10–15% band of your P99 requirement and cost is favorable, you can stay Hosted for initial rollout with a contractual latency SLA and automatic fallback to a reserved Dedicated pool during peak events. If Hosted cannot meet P99 in pilot, Dedicated will be the recommended path.

Concrete asks from your side:
- Approve the Hosted pilot (dates + a test window) or say you prefer we size Dedicated directly.
- Share a small representative request sample (anonymized) so we can simulate your token lengths and KV hit behavior.

I'll loop Vivek for the Dedicated sizing and Grace for the SOC2/logs details. If you want, we can also schedule a 30-min call to walk through the mutual action plan.

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: velocity_map_v1.pdf, latency-test-instructions.md

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Lee <tim.lee@velocityai.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@velocityai.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing suggestion for VelocityAI — initial recommendation

Looping in early sizing guidance. Quick notes before we run a formal perf test:

- Assumptions: model 7B-class (quantized), average prompt 40 tokens, response 30 tokens, KV cache hit 65%; target P99 <= 120ms for <=64 tokens.
- Recommendation: reserved Dedicated pool of 4x A100-equivalent GPU nodes (or 8x smaller Ampere instances depending on infra) with a 2-node standby for burst failover. This configuration aims to keep per-token service times low and avoid noisy-neighbor effects.
- Autoscale policy: instant burst to standby nodes for 30s windows, with warm-KV cache pre-warming during scheduled events.
- Cost note: estimated monthly committed spend: ~$42k–55k depending on cloud region and instance family. We'll provide a detailed breakout once we confirm model/precision.

Operational asks for procurement: SOC2 report link, expected SLA terms we can offer during pilot, and a 30-day canary/test window for throughput proof. Grace — can you confirm the log retention and tenancy isolation options we can commit to for a Dedicated contract?

-Vivek
Head of Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@velocityai.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@velocityai.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from demo — latency targets and QPS profile

Thanks — that approach makes sense. We're willing to run the Hosted pilot to get real P99 numbers, but only if the pilot includes:

- A defined rollback / automatic fallback to Dedicated if the P99 at 200 qps exceeds 150ms for more than two 5-minute windows during the pilot.
- A written timeline and cost estimate for the Dedicated configuration you suggested so procurement can prepare approvals in parallel.
- SOC2 evidence and confirmation that, should we choose Dedicated after pilot, logs and audit artifacts can be retained within our tenancy for 90 days.

I'll send an anonymized sample traffic file by EOD tomorrow. Please go ahead and schedule the pilot window for Oct 26–Nov 8 (2 weeks) unless you recommend different dates. Also please attach the mutual action plan as a Doc link so we can import to our procurement system.

On the rollback condition: we need the automated fallback behavior documented in the MAP (so procurement sees it). Aisha — can you confirm you'll include that clause?

—Tim
